section_summary: This section moves from correspondence about confiscated pearls and the occupation policy for Japanese fisheries to extensive discussion of Japanese fishing areas and Antarctic whaling. Allied officials debated food shortages, the size of Japan’s fishing fleet, Soviet objections, treaty obligations, and Norwegian and British concerns. The section ends with documents concerning authorization of a Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition for the 1946–47 season.

subfiles.title: Notice of confiscation to Joseph Goldstone
subfiles.from: John F. Stoskopf Jr., Criminal Investigation Division
subfiles.about: Goldstone is given sixty days to request return of a suitcase containing pearls.
subfiles.summary: Notice grants Goldstone sixty days to seek return of confiscated pearls.

subfiles.title: Reply to Joseph Goldstone about confiscated pearls
subfiles.from: R. W. Flournoy, Department of State
subfiles.about: The State Department says Army regulations govern the disposition of Goldstone’s pearls.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Goldstone’s letter and retains his enclosure.

subfiles.title: Press release sent to Miller Freeman
subfiles.about: Cale sends two copies of a release on Japanese fishing and aquatic industries during occupation.
subfiles.summary: Two copies of the occupation fisheries release are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Press release sent to Arthur Ponsford
subfiles.about: Cale sends Ponsford two copies of the occupation fisheries release.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter enclosing two copies of the fisheries release.

subfiles.title: Press release sent to Edward Allen
subfiles.about: Cale sends Allen two copies of the occupation fisheries release.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter enclosing two copies of the fisheries release.

subfiles.title: Van Camp Sea Food acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Phister thanks Cale for the press release and notes West Coast industry interest.
subfiles.summary: Phister reports strong West Coast interest in Japanese fishing developments.

subfiles.title: Pacific Salmon Commission acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Van Cleve thanks Cale for the Japanese fisheries policy release.
subfiles.summary: The release answers questions raised by the West Coast fishing industry.

subfiles.title: Referral of MacGowan and Goldstone investigation
subfiles.about: State sends Justice an investigation file to assess possible federal-law violations.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the MacGowan–Goldstone investigation and reports that seized pearls will be returned.

subfiles.title: Authorized Japanese whaling vessels
subfiles.about: Martin lists Japanese whalers and carrier vessels authorized to operate.
subfiles.summary: The letter provides names and gross tonnages of nine whalers and nine carriers.

subfiles.title: Alien Property Custodian referral of Steel proposal
subfiles.about: Shaulis forwards Mitchell Steel’s whaling proposal to State.
subfiles.summary: The custodian considers Steel’s proposal a State Department matter.

subfiles.title: Duplicate referral of Steel proposal
subfiles.about: A second copy forwards Steel’s whaling proposal to State.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the referral on page 87.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mitchell Steel
subfiles.about: Shaulis tells Steel his proposal has been sent to State for consideration.
subfiles.summary: The Alien Property Custodian disclaims jurisdiction and forwards the proposal.

subfiles.title: Proposal to finance Japanese whaling fleet
subfiles.about: Steel proposes financing and managing a Japanese whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Steel offers his decades of whaling experience to outfit and manage the fleet, seeking payment and a share of oil proceeds.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Bristol consular officer concerning Steel
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Bristol
subfiles.about: State supplies guidance for answering Steel’s proposed use of Japanese whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: No next-season decision had been made; distant-water operations might be leased to governments.

subfiles.title: Justice request for travel files
subfiles.about: Justice seeks passport and transportation files for MacGowan and Goldstone.
subfiles.summary: The Attorney General requests access to travel records to assess possible federal criminal violations.

subfiles.title: Halibut Commission acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Allen thanks Cale for the Japanese fisheries press release.
subfiles.summary: Allen acknowledges the release after returning from a two-month absence.

subfiles.title: State authorization for possible Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: State conditionally accepts renewed Japanese Antarctic whaling and requests notice of SCAP’s decision.
subfiles.summary: Whale oil would be allocated by the Combined Food Board, and approval would not settle future vessel disposition. State asks for evidence that Japanese operation can produce effectively and for inspection provisions meeting treaty obligations.

subfiles.title: Combined Food Board inquiry about factory ships
subfiles.about: Rossiter seeks information about two former Japanese factory ships held by the Navy.
subfiles.summary: The committee hopes the ships can be recovered for the next whaling season.

subfiles.title: Request to cable SCAP about former factory ships
subfiles.about: Hilldring proposes asking SCAP whether former Japanese factory vessels can be reconverted.
subfiles.summary: He asks War to transmit the attached draft cable if it has no objection.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on reconverting factory vessels
subfiles.about: The draft asks SCAP to identify two former Japanese whaling factory vessels.
subfiles.summary: One vessel may have become an aircraft carrier and another an oil tanker.

subfiles.title: File incorporation note
subfiles.about: Woodard sends material for incorporation into the file.
subfiles.summary: A short filing instruction made at Nicholas’s suggestion.

subfiles.title: Renewed Justice request for travel files
subfiles.about: Justice again requests access to MacGowan and Goldstone travel files.
subfiles.summary: The Attorney General says the investigation may have to close if State’s passport and transportation files yield no further evidence.

subfiles.title: State grants Justice access to relevant files
subfiles.about: State permits a Justice representative to examine relevant files.
subfiles.summary: The representative is directed to George Gray for help locating records.

subfiles.title: Transmission of fishing-area discussion
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: State sends its July 8 conversation memorandum about extending Japanese fishing areas.
subfiles.summary: The Political Adviser is invited to comment.

subfiles.title: Despatch routing slip
subfiles.about: The slip routes despatch 481.
subfiles.summary: Internal distribution record for despatch 481.

subfiles.title: Despatch 481 on fishing and whaling areas
subfiles.about: Atcheson reports Allied Council debate and Soviet opposition to enlarged Japanese fishing areas.
subfiles.summary: Derevyanko initially accepted a temporary extension but later relayed Soviet opposition, linking the proposal to fleet size. Atcheson argues that the extension is an emergency food measure distinct from decisions about the postwar fleet. Five supporting enclosures follow.

subfiles.title: SCAP staff memorandum and study on fishing-area extension
subfiles.about: SCAP requests council views on a proposed temporary enlargement of Japanese fishing grounds.
subfiles.summary: The study argues that Japan needs additional fishing grounds to increase food supplies and employ available vessels. It discusses seasonal fisheries, idle craft, and proposed boundaries, while maintaining that the extension would not endanger security.

subfiles.title: Earlier SCAP fishing-area directive
subfiles.about: An earlier directive defines permitted Japanese fishing and whaling areas.
subfiles.summary: Copy establishes area limits and restrictions for Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: Allied Council sixth-meeting minutes, fishing areas
subfiles.about: Council members discuss extending Japan’s authorized fishing and whaling area.
subfiles.summary: SCAP representatives present the proposal as a temporary response to severe food shortages and describe expected catches, vessels, fishing methods, and markets. Allied members question boundaries, precedent, fleet construction, and whether excess fish would be exported. Derevyanko asks detailed questions and initially says he has no objection in principle to a temporary arrangement.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1033: Area Authorized for Japanese Fishing and Whaling
subfiles.about: SCAP sets an expanded authorized area for Japanese fishing and whaling.
subfiles.summary: The directive specifies geographic limits and conditions, while reserving future decisions on jurisdiction and rights.

subfiles.title: Derevyanko’s objection to expanded fishing areas
subfiles.about: Derevyanko communicates Soviet opposition to expanding Japan’s fishing areas.
subfiles.summary: He argues existing grounds suffice and fleet size requires Allied and Far Eastern Commission decision.

subfiles.title: Atcheson’s reply to Derevyanko
subfiles.about: Atcheson defends the fishing-area extension as a temporary food-supply measure.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson says catch estimates are speculative and based partly on healthier prewar fisheries. He separates immediate use of available ships from the eventual decision on fleet size and emphasizes Japan’s food shortage and dependence on United States supplies.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission subcommittee discussion
subfiles.about: A subcommittee debates Soviet objections to enlarging Japanese fishing areas.
subfiles.summary: The Soviet representative contends that expansion would imply acceptance of a large fleet and excessive Japanese fish consumption. Flory argues that more fish could reduce food imports and that current decisions remain provisional. Members request further SCAP information on exports, diet, substitution for imports, and catches within existing areas.

subfiles.title: Soviet group statement on fishing-area extension
subfiles.about: The Soviet group argues that enlarging Japanese fishing areas is premature.
subfiles.summary: It links enlarged grounds to the unsettled question of Japan’s postwar fishing fleet.

subfiles.title: Draft recommendation on temporary fishing-area extension
subfiles.about: A draft recommends provisional expansion with safeguards for later decisions and Allied territory.
subfiles.summary: Extension would be provisional and require consent for fishing near Allied territory.

subfiles.title: Norwegian Ambassador’s inquiry on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: The Norwegian Ambassador objects to renewed Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Penfield records Norway’s conservation and commercial concerns and suggests discussion with Far Eastern Commission members.

subfiles.title: Flory memorandum on responding to Norway
subfiles.about: Flory proposes awaiting SCAP’s whaling decision before responding to Norway.
subfiles.summary: He also suggests addressing vessel limits at the planned international whaling conference.

subfiles.title: Draft telegram seeking SCAP whaling decision
subfiles.about: The draft asks SCAP to report its decision and forecast Japanese whaling effectiveness.
subfiles.summary: Prepared after Norway expressed opposition to future Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: Penfield request for fisheries views
subfiles.about: Penfield requests views on the attached Norwegian whaling conversation.
subfiles.summary: A brief request for departmental comment.

subfiles.title: Copy of Norwegian Ambassador telephone memorandum
subfiles.about: A second copy records Norway’s objection to renewed Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate, more legible copy of the memorandum on page 132.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation on fishing-area extension
subfiles.about: A poorly legible memorandum concerns committee discussion of the fishing-area extension.
subfiles.summary: Most substantive text is unreadable in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Whitman proposal to query SCAP on whaling
subfiles.about: Whitman urges a query to SCAP before further discussion with Norway.
subfiles.summary: A proposed message asks for SCAP’s decision and expected effectiveness of Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: Telegram 413 requesting SCAP whaling report
subfiles.about: State asks SCAP to report its decision and production assessment before State answers Norway.
subfiles.summary: The message cites Norwegian opposition and requests prompt notice.

subfiles.title: Note on channel for SCAP telegram
subfiles.about: A handwritten note recommends sending the proposed whaling message as a State telegram.
subfiles.summary: The writer cites State’s primary interest in the matter.

subfiles.title: SCAP report on planned Antarctic expedition
subfiles.to: Secretary of State via War Department
subfiles.about: SCAP reports plans to authorize two factory ships and twelve catcher vessels.
subfiles.summary: SCAP estimates catches and whale-product yields for 1946–47, expects Japanese crews to outperform pooled operations, and promises inspection provisions.

subfiles.title: Corrected copy of SCAP whaling report
subfiles.about: A corrected copy gives details of SCAP’s planned Antarctic whaling authorization.
subfiles.summary: It clarifies expected production, Japanese operating advantages, and applicable international whaling agreements.

subfiles.title: Correction of SCAP telegram number
subfiles.about: The branch corrects the serial designation of the August 5 SCAP message.
subfiles.summary: The message number is corrected to 340.

subfiles.title: Urgent routing slip
subfiles.about: An urgent slip directs material to the Fisheries and Wildlife Branch.
subfiles.summary: Internal routing instruction.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation with Knut Lykke
subfiles.about: Flory explains the conditions on Japanese Antarctic whaling authorization to Lykke.
subfiles.summary: He describes treaty compliance, allocation of whale oil, and the provisional nature of approval. Lykke objects to the lack of advance notice, the potential military use of whaling ships, and pressure on the international catch limit.

subfiles.title: Telegram on fishing-area questions and fisheries policy
subfiles.about: State seeks answers to Far Eastern Commission questions and a broad fisheries assessment.
subfiles.summary: The telegram asks about fish exports, substitution for imported food, calories, and catches in existing grounds. It also seeks SCAP analysis of vessel construction, whaling, foreign exchange, and possible effects on Pacific fisheries.

subfiles.title: Flory guidance for reply to British inquiry
subfiles.about: Flory supplies conditions of Japanese Antarctic whaling approval for use in a British reply.
subfiles.summary: The conditions cover treaties, whale-oil allocation, and later policy decisions.

subfiles.title: Emmerson memorandum to Vincent on British concern
subfiles.about: Emmerson relays Flory’s suggested response and anticipates a strong British objection.
subfiles.summary: He notes a pending request for SCAP verification and operational details.

subfiles.title: Emmerson record of Graves telephone inquiry
subfiles.about: Graves questions whether Japanese whaling is compatible with Far Eastern Commission policy.
subfiles.summary: Graves argues that Allied-area restrictions and wartime abrogation of agreements may bar Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: Additional corrected copy of SCAP whaling report
subfiles.about: Another copy reports the planned Japanese Antarctic expedition and expected yields.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the corrected telegram on page 142.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Japanese whaling directive
subfiles.about: A badly degraded telegram concerns authorization and direction of Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Its operational details cannot be reliably recovered from the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Distribution note
subfiles.about: A note requests notice if a despatch is distributed outside the Department.
subfiles.summary: Internal distribution instruction.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for Tokyo despatch
subfiles.about: The slip routes a Tokyo despatch for action and copies.
subfiles.summary: Internal distribution record.

subfiles.title: Despatch 558 on Antarctic whaling directive
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tokyo sends SCAP’s staff study and directives on Japanese Antarctic whaling.
subfiles.summary: The cover despatch refers to earlier notification and lists three sets of enclosed documents.

subfiles.title: Concurrences for Antarctic whaling staff study
subfiles.about: A concurrence page lists officials who approved the Antarctic whaling staff study.
subfiles.summary: Lists State, diplomatic, naval, and military staff concurrences.
